_readme: EC hardware registry: every EC address, register encoding, address region and driver
IOCTL the product touches, declared exactly once. Consumed at build time by
regenerated when this file is newer; the Core suite pins that the committed artifact
matches this file). Do NOT add an EC number to product code: add it here.
SCOPE: wire encodings only (addresses, register bit/value encodings, address regions,
driver IOCTLs). Domain rules and product limits (watt ranges, thresholds, hysteresis,
percentages) stay in the codecs - they are policy, not wiring.
EVIDENCE: every entry names where the number came from. Provenance levels used by this
codebase, strongest first: 'probe' (field-verified on the lab box), 'uniwill-laptop-driver'
(Linux kernel module for the same EC), 'tuxedo-drivers uniwill_interfaces.h', 'MechControl
its registry is a hypothesis here, never proof), 'declared in EcEngine.cs' (no provenance
platform: all | amd | intel (EcPlatform vocabulary). access: rw | ro | wo (omitted = rw).
Duplicate addresses under different names are legal: the same byte answers to several
domains (0x0742 is a support byte AND the battery gate status; 0x0402 is the mux state
AND the design-capacity low byte). Names must be unique.
